clippings.quote: We usually discover this after we’ve committed. Rather than back out, we push on. In Africa, while shooting a sequence for Dead Reckoning Part Two, he came up with an idea that I told him could not be done, simply because no camera rig existed that could capture it. By that afternoon, our team had built it.
clippings.title: Meet Christopher McQuarrie, wingman to Tom Cruise’s death-defying maverick
clippings.context: Same Q&A, asked whether Cruise ever had an idea too complex to do; the film was then titled Dead Reckoning Part Two.

clippings.speaker: Christopher McQuarrie
clippings.quote: At the start of this movie, I said to Tom, 'What do you want to do?' … He said, 'I want to drive a motorcycle off of a cliff. What do you want to do?' And I said, 'I want to wreck a train.'
clippings.film: Mission: Impossible – Dead Reckoning Part One
clippings.title: ‘M:I 7’ Director Was Determined to ‘Wreck’ a 70-Ton Train Like Buster Keaton
clippings.context: IndieWire quoting McQuarrie's Entertainment Weekly interview about how he and Cruise picked their dream stunts.

clippings.speaker: Tom Cruise
clippings.quote: That's McQ [Christopher McQuarrie]. McQ designed that whole thing and we had to build the train for that. … But, as a kid, I played with trains. McQ played with trains. We always wanted to throw a train off a cliff or blow it up.
clippings.film: Mission: Impossible – Dead Reckoning Part One
clippings.title: Tom Cruise Dreamed of Throwing a Train Off a Cliff as a Kid, So He Did in ‘Mission: Impossible 7’
clippings.context: Q&A with Ben Felderstein, answering the first question about the film's train sequence.

clippings.speaker: Tom Cruise
clippings.quote: You see what's right in front of him. McQ has a tremendous ability to be able to do that. And he has a tremendous ability to be able to write for actors.
clippings.film: Mission: Impossible – Dead Reckoning Part One
clippings.title: Tom Cruise Dreamed of Throwing a Train Off a Cliff as a Kid, So He Did in ‘Mission: Impossible 7’
clippings.context: Same Q&A, on how the franchise avoids feeling repetitive by building each film around what the actors do well.

clippings.speaker: Tom Cruise
clippings.quote: You look at McQ [Christopher McQuarrie], McQ has such an understanding and appreciation of rhythm as an editor. He just has a brilliance with rhythm [when] he and I edit the film, it has to have a natural rhythm and you feel it. And then the icing is the score.
clippings.title: “I never made a movie to just go make a movie, it was always an exploration of filmmaking”: our world exclusive interview with Tom Cruise
clippings.context: Interview with Isabel Stevens for the BFI Fellowship, on why he dislikes editing to music.

clippings.speaker: Spike Lee
clippings.quote: Very much so. I think it's evident by the work we've done. And we have acquired sort of like a shorthand. You know, we do most of our discussion, rehearsals, but we're on the set, we know what we have to do. So there's not a lot of need for a whole lot of talking.
clippings.title: A Conversation with Spike Lee
clippings.context: Lee talked with Scott Simon on NPR about Inside Man, his fourth film with Washington.

clippings.speaker: Spike Lee
clippings.quote: Same way a coach, you're not gonna let everybody take the last shot when the game is on the line. In a movie, you put the ball in Denzel's hands.
clippings.title: A Conversation with Spike Lee
clippings.context: Lee talked with Scott Simon on NPR about Inside Man, his fourth film with Washington.

clippings.speaker: Spike Lee
clippings.quote: I've become a better director working with Mr. Denzel Washington. … It's not about just what's on the script. It has to be deeper than that.
clippings.title: Spike Lee and Denzel Washington on a Reunion Making “Highest 2 Lowest”
clippings.context: Joint interview of Lee and Washington by David Remnick before Highest 2 Lowest opened; the page notes the transcript was produced on a rush deadline.

clippings.speaker: Denzel Washington
clippings.quote: When I started acting, there were two or three actors that I followed. De Niro, Hoffman, Pacino, the filmmakers that made those films never called me. I was never asked to be in any of their films. When Spike called me, we developed a relationship, and we made our own films.
clippings.title: Spike Lee and Denzel Washington on a Reunion Making “Highest 2 Lowest”
clippings.context: Washington on why he and Lee built a partnership beginning with Mo' Better Blues (1990), in the same joint interview.

clippings.speaker: Denzel Washington
clippings.quote: Which is why I call Spike, Trust. I trust Spike completely. … I completely, 1000% trust Spike and I do my part and he does the rest.
clippings.title: Spike Lee and Denzel Washington on a Reunion Making “Highest 2 Lowest”
clippings.context: Washington on the shorthand built over five films, in the same joint interview.

clippings.speaker: Denzel Washington
clippings.quote: In this case, the script came to me first. I hoped that Spike would be interested in, so I called him up, he said, ‘Send it to me.’ He read it, he said, ‘Let's make it,’ and here we are.
clippings.title: Spike Lee and Denzel Washington on a Reunion Making “Highest 2 Lowest”
clippings.context: Washington on how Highest 2 Lowest came together, in the same joint interview.

clippings.speaker: Samuel L. Jackson
clippings.quote: But Quentin would say, no, take your time. And I'd do it again. I'd count to, like, five, and he'd say, no, no, no. … Which consequently led me to that almost, you know, 20-second pause in that film that he left in it. … But Quentin trusts audiences like I do.
clippings.title: Celebrating movie icons: Samuel Jackson
clippings.context: Terry Gross interview recorded in 2000, rebroadcast 2024-09-02; Jackson recalls shooting the Jackie Brown van scene.

clippings.speaker: Samuel L. Jackson
clippings.quote: He knows the movies that we like. I tend to go on location with about 30 Hong Kong films — I have a lot of Asian crime films in my trailer just to pass the time. Every time he’d pass my trailer he’d ask, ‘what are you watching now?’ and we’ll talk about it. We had long conversations about those movies. We tend to watch the same kind of bullshit. Entertainment.
clippings.title: Samuel L. Jackson Lets Loose On ‘Django’, Tarantino, Slavery, Oscars And Golden Globes – Interview
clippings.context: Deadline interview during the Django Unchained release, on shared taste in genre movies.

clippings.speaker: Samuel L. Jackson
clippings.quote: We are the constant — we’re the base flavor for that bouillabaisse he makes, we’re the tomato consommé or whatever.
clippings.title: ‘Hateful Eight’ Star Samuel L. Jackson Says He’s the Base in Quentin Tarantino’s Bouillabaisse
clippings.context: Q&A on what it takes to be the right actor for Tarantino films, around The Hateful Eight release.

clippings.speaker: Quentin Tarantino
clippings.quote: I love him because nobody says my dialogue quite the way Sam Jackson does. It's not poetry but it's poetic. It's not song, but it's musical and he sings it. It's not stand-up comedy but it has a comedic rhythm…
clippings.title: Pieces of eight
clippings.context: Tarantino chatting with the writer after The Hateful Eight press conference.

clippings.speaker: Quentin Tarantino
clippings.quote: Not only has it become easy to write for him, it’s become hard not to write for him.
clippings.title: Quentin Tarantino Defends Violence in ‘Hateful Eight,’ No Cell Phone Policy; Reveals Why Samuel L. Jackson Is His Muse
clippings.context: Variety 'Contenders Conversations' interview on The Hateful Eight; caption quotes Tarantino on Jackson.

clippings.speaker: Quentin Tarantino
clippings.quote: I remember after I gave Sam Jackson the first draft of the script, I go to him, I go, ‘What's your favourite part of it?’ He goes, ‘I like when I start figuring shit out, and I turn into Hercule Négrô.’
clippings.title: Interview: THE HATEFUL EIGHT Los Angeles And New York Press Conferences
clippings.context: Tarantino at Hateful Eight press events (Dec 2015), as transcribed by ScreenAnarchy.

clippings.speaker: Martin Scorsese
clippings.quote: He has range. He keeps growing. He also has a lot of courage. I know he'll go to places that other people might pull back from… I've been working with him over the years he's been growing as a person. He's maturing from a young kid to a young man. As he changes in life, he's changing on film.
clippings.title: Martin Scorsese Details Working With Leonardo DiCaprio and How He's Matured as an Actor (Exclusive)
clippings.context: Scorsese to ET at the New York premiere of Killers of the Flower Moon.

clippings.speaker: Martin Scorsese
clippings.quote: And then finally Leo said, ‘If I play Ernest, we could turn it upside down and go in from the ground level.’ And I said, ‘Absolutely.’ So DiCaprio was the first driver of that change. Absolutely.
clippings.title: Martin Scorsese, the Interview: On Reframing 'Killers,' Subverting DiCaprio's Star Power — and 'The Wager'
clippings.context: Scorsese recounts how DiCaprio's decision to play Ernest Burkhart rather than the FBI agent reshaped the script.

clippings.speaker: Martin Scorsese
clippings.quote: We have this ability to collaborate together, and it's based on trust and love. We go to places sometimes that at times feel almost impossible.
clippings.title: Why Leonardo DiCaprio and Martin Scorsese 'Debate for Months' Before Every Movie
clippings.context: Scorsese on stage with DiCaprio at TIME's 'A Year in TIME' event, as they prepare their seventh film together.

clippings.speaker: Leonardo DiCaprio
clippings.quote: I know the trust level has built over the years. (Scorsese) has taught me not only about being a better actor, but the history of cinema and the importance of cinema as an art form.
clippings.title: SBIFF: Double Dose – Martin Scorsese and Leonardo DiCaprio share the stage at SBIFF
clippings.context: DiCaprio, in a Variety interview earlier that week (during The Wolf of Wall Street press run), quoted in Ted Mills's SBIFF report.

clippings.speaker: Leonardo DiCaprio
clippings.quote: Well, in a lot of ways these two men that we're speaking to have been like cinematic father figures to me… He told Marty about me, and I've gotten to do six films with him now. And here we are 30 years later.
clippings.title: Leonardo DiCaprio Views Martin Scorsese and Robert De Niro as Special 'Father Figures'
clippings.context: DiCaprio at a Nov. 15, 2023 press conference, speaking of Scorsese and Robert De Niro together ('these two men'; 'Marty' is Scorsese).

clippings.speaker: Leonardo DiCaprio
clippings.quote: Marty's very obsessive as a filmmaker, he thinks about every single detail. Over the years, I've learned the times when there's a malleability and ways to pivot in the storyline, but I've also learned the times where you have a specific shot list.
clippings.title: Why Leonardo DiCaprio and Martin Scorsese 'Debate for Months' Before Every Movie
clippings.context: DiCaprio in conversation with Scorsese at TIME's 'A Year in TIME' event.

clippings.speaker: Song Kang-ho
clippings.quote: When we first started together, it was over 20 years ago. I was a novice actor in his second film. Back then, we were both new to the craft as a director and actor. After twenty years, it's much more than that. We're now friends.
clippings.title: Interview: Song Kang Ho and Park So Dam On 'Parasite' and Becoming A Family
clippings.context: Song on how his relationship with Bong has changed since Memories of Murder, during Parasite press (translated).

clippings.speaker: Song Kang-ho
clippings.quote: I met the two men who would later become master filmmakers. They were like college students with crop hair. We had a cup of tea and parted without saying a word about movies. Later, they told me that they had wanted to see me to cast me in a film.
clippings.title: [Interview] Song Kang-ho, "The Title Is 'Parasite,' But the Film Is about Symbiosis"
clippings.context: Song recalls his first meeting with Bong (then an assistant director on Motel Cactus), in a Seoul interview before Parasite's release (translated).

clippings.speaker: Song Kang-ho
clippings.quote: What I really like about him is his realism; his worldview on the society and the people that we live with. I feel like his views have become more relentless, persistent, and meticulous over the years, and I think Parasite is really the concentrated result of all those years of effort.
clippings.title: PARASITE Interview: Acting Legend Song Kang-ho on his "Relentless" Relationship with Bong Joon-ho
clippings.context: Song answers what is special about their collaboration from Memories of Murder through Parasite (translated).

clippings.speaker: Bong Joon Ho
clippings.quote: I don't think of it as me directing actors. I'm just entering Song's world, the vast universe that he occupies. He has a unique rhythm and tempo. Working with Song is something I feel confident in.
clippings.title: Clutch For A Villain: An Interview With Bong Joon-Ho And Song Kang-Ho
clippings.context: Bong on directing Song, in a joint interview at the Locarno Film Festival (translated).

clippings.speaker: Bong Joon Ho
clippings.quote: he acts with insight with every small detail and nuance, and never goes against the big context that surrounds the film. When he plays a scene, I think the audience is more convinced that something like that could happen.
clippings.title: "All Characters in 'Parasite' Are in the Gray Zone." Bong Joon-ho on the War of the Classes in His New Masterpiece
clippings.context: Bong, asked why he keeps returning to Song, in a New York interview (translated).

clippings.speaker: Bong Joon Ho
clippings.quote: For my second movie, 'Memories of Murder,' I thought, I'd really love to work with Song Kang-ho, but my debut had been a disaster. I thought I was about to get chased out of the industry, and he was a star. But he remembered that meeting fondly.
clippings.publication: Bong Joon Ho: Dissident Cinema (Karen Han, Abrams)
clippings.title: How Bong Joon Ho Discovered Song Kang-ho for 'Memories of Murder' — and Made Them a Dream Team
clippings.context: Book excerpt quoting Bong ('Bong has said') on why he wanted Song for his second film; the original interview is not identified.

clippings.speaker: Pedro Almodóvar
clippings.quote: Penélope has done ballet when she was younger and that gave her a very gracious and light way of walking. I wanted her to have more weight, so you could feel the sense of gravity attaching her to the Earth.
clippings.title: Women are more interesting: Talking with Pedro Almodóvar and Penélope Cruz
clippings.context: Almodóvar explains how he reshaped Cruz's physicality for Volver; interview at the film's 2006 release (translation not stated).

clippings.speaker: Penélope Cruz
clippings.quote: I was so happy that he called me again and gave me the most challenging, difficult, complex character of my career up to now. When I read it, it was more than what I dreamt about. He was actually my biggest motivation to becoming an actress.
clippings.title: Interview with Penelope Cruz
clippings.context: Q&A at a Tribeca Cinema Series advance screening; she speaks of Volver as the new film (Tribeca's page is dated Nov 2007, the screening was presumably 2006).

clippings.speaker: Penélope Cruz
clippings.quote: I have fear, always on the set. Insecurity to the point where the first week I always think I could be fired. I think that’s a fear most actors have. But Pedro can intimidate me more than anybody. Because I care so much about him and I don’t want to disappoint him.
clippings.title: Penelope Cruz talks Broken Embraces - RT Interview
clippings.context: Interview at Cannes 2009 for their fourth film together (page later updated in 2015).

clippings.speaker: Pedro Almodóvar
clippings.quote: With Penélope, before we begin shooting, she needs to really rehearse a lot so she really feels that she’s able to enter into that role. That’s not the case with Antonio Banderas, it’s very much about directing him in the moment.
clippings.title: Pedro Almodóvar discusses drugs, Penélope Cruz and not understanding camp
clippings.context: Asked about his long working relationship with Cruz while promoting Pain and Glory in London (translation not stated).

clippings.speaker: Pedro Almodóvar
clippings.quote: The nature of muses is not only to inspire you, but also to give you confidence in yourself
clippings.title: Penélope Cruz Takes on Her Dream Role for Pedro Almodóvar
clippings.context: Almodóvar to the writer by phone from Madrid, for W's Directors Issue photo story starring Cruz (translation not stated).

clippings.speaker: Pedro Almodóvar
clippings.quote: She needs to feel what she’s doing. But because she’s so emotional, every time she read the script she would be overcome and would start crying. At first, I let her cry all she wanted, but then I dedicated myself to draining her of her tears, until the very end.
clippings.title: Pedro Almodovar and Penelope Cruz on Pain, Friendship and Sexy Mothers
clippings.context: On directing Cruz through the long rehearsal period for Parallel Mothers (translation not stated).

clippings.speaker: Penélope Cruz
clippings.quote: I love him and I trust him 100% of the time, and at the same time I’m scared. Not scared of him. I’m scared of… I don’t want to disappoint him. And I know he’s going to be honest and he’s going to be tough. And that is a great fear to have on the set. I’d much rather have that than have somebody that always tells you everything is right, because we know it’s not.
clippings.title: 'Parallel Mothers' star Penelope Cruz on her intense working relationship with Pedro Almodovar
clippings.context: Cruz on how their friendship and working relationship differ on set, awards-season interview for Parallel Mothers.

clippings.speaker: Penélope Cruz
clippings.quote: He literally had to pick me up from the floor, because I could not come out of the fiction. It took me a while and he got worried. He said, ‘No, but why it has to be this way? I want you to do the same thing, but not suffer.’
clippings.title: 'Parallel Mothers' star Penelope Cruz on her intense working relationship with Pedro Almodovar
clippings.context: Cruz recalls a Parallel Mothers shoot day when she could not shake a devastating scene.

clippings.speaker: Christopher Miller
clippings.quote: The reason this collaboration is successful is because each of us respects and values the other person and what he brings. And we’re each like a life preserver rather than a weight. The second it feels like a nuisance, it’s doomed.
clippings.title: Dynamic Duo
clippings.context: Answering how their collaboration has evolved, in a joint Q&A with fellow Dartmouth alumnus Jake Tapper (interview held May 20, 2019).

clippings.speaker: Phil Lord
clippings.quote: Our first 10 years we would have our frustrations, but the work was always better when it was the two of us. It’s just more fun to do it with your buddy, and it’s more interesting to be challenged.
clippings.title: Dynamic Duo
clippings.context: Same joint Q&A, on how the partnership has changed over time.

clippings.speaker: Christopher Miller
clippings.quote: We’re like brothers, where we fight and love each other and respect each other. We’ve had such a long history together. We’ve known each other for 20 years.
clippings.title: '22 Jump Street' Directors Phil Lord and Chris Miller Discuss How Friendship Turned Into Comedy Gold
clippings.context: Joint interview ahead of 22 Jump Street's release, on the trouble of two directors sharing one film.

clippings.speaker: Phil Lord
clippings.quote: It takes just as long to do another take [as] it does to argue about whether you should do another take. Just do one. And I trust this guy if he has something that he wants to do, we should just do it.
clippings.title: '22 Jump Street' Directors Phil Lord and Chris Miller Discuss How Friendship Turned Into Comedy Gold
clippings.context: Same joint interview, on settling disagreements on set.

clippings.speaker: Christopher Miller
clippings.quote: During college, we were friends, we would help each other on each other's films, but Phil's films were his and my films were mine, and we'd never been in an equal partnership where neither one was the boss. It was a lot to figure out how to be in a partnership, which was really challenging. It's like a marriage, and luckily we stuck with it, because we weren't very good at it at the beginning.
clippings.title: Phil Lord and Chris Miller Prove the Power of Partnership With Variety's Creative Impact in Animation Award
clippings.context: Variety profile on the pair receiving its Creative Impact in Animation Award, recalling their first year as Disney-era partners.

clippings.speaker: Phil Lord
clippings.quote: One of the things that's neat about being partners for so long is the partnership grows to accommodate a lot of different facets of each of us… You have to allow for each partner to grow and develop and do their thing. It's been really lovely to be able to support Chris, and we were on the set together the whole time…
clippings.title: Chris Miller And Phil Lord On The Afterparty And The More Ambitious Spider-Verse Sequels - Exclusive Interview
clippings.context: Exclusive interview on Miller creating and directing The Afterparty while Lord supported him.

clippings.speaker: Ben Affleck
clippings.quote: That’s why we stayed friends: because we lie for each other in crucial moments. It gets you through a development meeting, I can tell you that.
clippings.title: New Again: Ben Affleck
clippings.context: Joint interview with Ingrid Sischy as Good Will Hunting was about to open; the page is Interview's 2014 online republication of the December 1997 piece.

clippings.speaker: Ben Affleck
clippings.quote: Matt and I had identical interests, so whether we ended up successful or making hot dogs at Dodgers games, we knew we’d end up doing the same sort of thing. The remaining friends part was pretty consistent. We saw each other all the time, we talked on the phone all the time.
clippings.title: New Again: Ben Affleck
clippings.context: Answering whether he and Damon were sure they'd stay friends after high school and end up writing together.

clippings.speaker: Ben Affleck
clippings.quote: It was a very gracious and kind gesture that’s characteristic of how Matt’s treated me, and this friendship, his whole life … It’s a testament to why we are still friends.
clippings.title: A duo once more, Ben Affleck, Matt Damon come up for 'Air'
clippings.context: On Damon's support when Affleck directed him for the first time, in an AP profile by Jake Coyle.

clippings.speaker: Matt Damon
clippings.quote: Ben’s too modest to tell you this, but he’s the most well-read person I know. He’s certainly a lot smarter than I am.
clippings.title: New Again: Ben Affleck
clippings.context: Teasing Affleck, who had just joked about dropping out of college, in the same joint interview.

clippings.speaker: Matt Damon
clippings.quote: Once we started, we really got into a groove. While I was away, I’d write and fax the stuff to Ben, and Ben would fax stuff to me, and we’d write on and edit each other’s faxes.
clippings.title: New Again: Ben Affleck
clippings.context: Describing how they co-wrote the Good Will Hunting screenplay when apart.

clippings.speaker: Matt Damon
clippings.quote: After my dad passed in 2017 — and Ben was very, very close with him — it changed something in us, I think … You start to see the end game and you start to feel like, ‘I want to make every second count. I don’t want to fritter away time anymore.’
clippings.title: Matt Damon Says His Friendship with Ben Affleck 'Changed' After His Dad Died
clippings.context: TODAY quotes Damon from the July 21, 2023 episode of 'Who's Talking to Chris Wallace?', on why he and Affleck began working together more often.
